summary.text: Patient 1 of the 11-patient case series is listed in Table 2 as male (sex column M) with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed at age 9 years and a disease duration of 15 months. Previous treatments before tocilizumab were NSAIDs, methotrexate, corticosteroids.

Tocilizumab was given by intravenous infusion for 5 months, with a visual analogue scale of 10 before treatment and 2 after. Tuberculosis evaluation was done beforehand, and TST and IGRA were negative afterwards with no tuberculosis observed, and CRP was below 3.1 mg/l after treatment. The patient did not die during treatment.

For this sJIA patient the series reports that the systemic signs completely disappeared after a few days following tocilizumab, with the improvement maintained, and that clinical remission was achieved following commencement of tocilizumab.

summary.text: Patient 2 of the 11-patient case series is listed in Table 2 as female (sex column F) with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed at age 10 years and a disease duration of 58 months. Previous treatments before tocilizumab were NSAIDs, methotrexate, corticosteroids, canakinumab.

Tocilizumab was given by intravenous infusion for 31 months, with a visual analogue scale of 10 before treatment and 3 after. Tuberculosis evaluation was done beforehand, and TST and IGRA were negative afterwards with no tuberculosis observed, and CRP was below 3.1 mg/l after treatment. The patient did not die during treatment.

For this sJIA patient the series reports that the systemic signs completely disappeared after a few days following tocilizumab, with the improvement maintained, and that clinical remission was achieved following commencement of tocilizumab.

summary.text: Patient 4 of the 11-patient case series is listed in Table 2 as female (sex column F) with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed at age 4 years and a disease duration of 21 months. Previous treatments before tocilizumab were NSAIDs, methotrexate, corticosteroids, canakinumab.

Tocilizumab was given by intravenous infusion for 12 months, with a visual analogue scale of 10 before treatment and 0 after. Tuberculosis evaluation was done beforehand, and TST and IGRA were negative afterwards with no tuberculosis observed, and CRP was below 3.1 mg/l after treatment. The patient did not die during treatment.

For this sJIA patient the series reports that the systemic signs completely disappeared after a few days following tocilizumab, with the improvement maintained, and that clinical remission was achieved following commencement of tocilizumab.

summary.text: Patient 5 of the 11-patient case series is listed in Table 2 as female (sex column F) with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed at age 13 years and a disease duration of 32 months. Previous treatments before tocilizumab were methotrexate, corticosteroids, canakinumab.

Tocilizumab was given by intravenous infusion for 13 months, with a visual analogue scale of 6 before treatment and 2 after. Tuberculosis evaluation was done beforehand, and TST and IGRA were negative afterwards with no tuberculosis observed, and CRP was below 3.1 mg/l after treatment. The patient did not die during treatment.

For this sJIA patient the series reports that the systemic signs completely disappeared after a few days following tocilizumab, with the improvement maintained, and that clinical remission was achieved following commencement of tocilizumab.

summary.text: Patient 8 of the 11-patient case series is listed in Table 2 as female (sex column F) with polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed at age 3 years and a disease duration of 118 months. Previous treatments before tocilizumab were NSAIDs, methotrexate, Anti-TNF.

Tocilizumab was given by intravenous infusion for 17 months, with a visual analogue scale of 10 before treatment and 3 after. Tuberculosis evaluation was done beforehand, and TST and IGRA were negative afterwards with no tuberculosis observed, and CRP was below 3.1 mg/l after treatment. The patient did not die during treatment. Listed possible adverse effects: Nasopharyngitis.

summary.text: Patient 9 of the 11-patient case series is listed in Table 2 as male (sex column M) with polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed at age 1 years and a disease duration of 70 months. Previous treatments before tocilizumab were NSAIDs, methotrexate, corticosteroids, Anti-TNF.

Tocilizumab was given by intravenous infusion for 17 months, with a visual analogue scale of 8 before treatment and 2 after. Tuberculosis evaluation was done beforehand, and TST and IGRA were negative afterwards with no tuberculosis observed, and CRP was below 3.1 mg/l after treatment. The patient did not die during treatment. Listed possible adverse effects: Nasopharyngitis, epistaxis.
